verdict.rationale: Honeybadger records deployments via an API endpoint, the CLI, and Capistrano, and links each revision to a GitHub or GitLab diff since the last deploy. It also says deploy tracking lets you 'correlate code changes with errors', and errors can be searched with occurred.after:'last deploy'. That gives coarse deploy-to-error correlation, but nothing shows an issue displaying the release it first appeared in or naming a suspect commit. Missing for 10: per-issue first-seen release, suspect-commit attribution, commit association on individual errors, independent hands-on corroboration.
